summary: The note describes the iPLEDGE program, an FDA requirement that took effect on March 1, 2006. Under it, patients, doctors and pharmacists must register and use a web site to receive, prescribe or dispense the medication. The note says the program has reduced pregnant women's exposure to the drug but has been criticized as overly complicated.
one_line: iPLEDGE is an FDA-mandated web-based registration program, effective March 1, 2006, for patients, doctors and pharmacists handling a restricted medication.
key_facts: iPLEDGE patients, their doctors and their pharmacists are required by the FDA to register and use a web site to receive, prescribe or dispense the medication.
The iPLEDGE registration requirement took effect as of March 1, 2006.
The iPLEDGE program has reduced exposure of pregnant women to the drug.
The iPLEDGE program has been criticized for being overly complicated.
